Green Gate Advisory provides integrated climate and environmental advisory services to help clients understand their obligations, assess strategic opportunities and develop credible pathways to implementation.

faqs.q: Can Green Gate Advisory help develop a carbon credit project?
faqs.a: Green Gate Advisory’s proposed service scope includes opportunity screening, feasibility, methodology assessment, project documentation and MRV planning, as well as support through relevant validation, registration and commercialisation processes. Actual requirements and outcomes depend on project eligibility, programme rules and independent review.

faqs.q: Does Green Gate Advisory guarantee funding or carbon credit issuance?

faqs.q: What is an emissions trading system (ETS)?
faqs.a: An emissions trading system is a carbon-pricing mechanism in which regulated entities may need to manage emissions allowances under the rules of a particular scheme. Scope, obligations and procedures differ by jurisdiction.

faqs.q: How does Article 6 advisory relate to compliance carbon pricing?
faqs.a: Article 6 of the Paris Agreement provides mechanisms for bilateral cooperation (Article 6.2) and multilateral centralized crediting (Article 6.4). Organisations and governments require structured advisory on corresponding adjustments, authorization frameworks, and national registry integration to avoid double counting.

cbam.lead: Prepare for CBAM-related requirements with product screening, embedded emissions data, supplier engagement, reporting processes and carbon-cost risk assessment.
cbam.intro: The European Union’s Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) can create new data, reporting and carbon-cost considerations for certain imported goods and the companies that produce or export them. Green Gate Advisory helps businesses assess potential exposure, organise emissions information and establish a practical readiness plan based on current applicable rules.

faqs.q: What is CBAM and why might exporters need to assess it?
faqs.a: The EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism is a regulatory framework concerning the embedded emissions of certain imported goods. Exporters and supply-chain businesses may need to determine whether their products and commercial relationships fall within the applicable rules and what data or reporting processes are required.

faqs.q: Does advisory support replace official EU declarant registration?
faqs.a: No. Importers into the EU must be registered as authorized CBAM declarants with the European Commission and national competent authorities. Green Gate Advisory provides technical analysis, embedded emissions calculation support, and compliance readiness planning.

faqs.a: A climate advisory consultancy helps public and private organisations understand climate-related risks, regulations, policy options and implementation pathways. For public bodies, support covers NDC planning, adaptation strategies, carbon pricing, and MRV frameworks.

faqs.a: Robust MRV systems enable governments to track emissions baselines, policy impacts, and NDC progress transparently, providing the technical data required for Biennial Transparency Reports (BTRs).

faqs.q: What is involved in Scope 1, 2 and 3 greenhouse gas accounting?
faqs.a: Scope 1 covers direct emissions from owned operations. Scope 2 covers indirect emissions from purchased electricity and heat. Scope 3 covers broader value-chain emissions, including purchased goods, logistics, and product use.

faqs.q: How does Green Gate Advisory support TCFD and ISSB reporting readiness?
faqs.a: We help companies identify climate risks and opportunities across governance, strategy, risk management, and metrics/targets, preparing structured data and internal processes for formal disclosures.
